crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Satellite Imagery
children.blurb: Satellite imagery as alternative data means using pictures of the Earth's surface, taken from orbit, as an input to economic and business analysis rather than as a map or a photograph.

children.name: Card Transaction Data
children.blurb: Card transaction data covers the records generated when a payment card is used, including the merchant, the amount, the timestamp and a category code, with the cardholder identity removed or masked.

children.name: Sensor and Shipping Data
children.blurb: Sensor and shipping data covers the physical signals that track goods and vessels as they move: automatic identification system (AIS) broadcasts from ships, port call records, container and terminal throughput, satellite imagery of vessels and storage tanks, and telemetry from trucks, rail and warehouse equipment.

children.name: Mobile Location Data
children.blurb: Mobile location data is the record of where a phone has been, inferred from signals such as GPS, Wi-Fi connections and cell tower handoffs.

children.name: Web Data Collection
children.blurb: Web data collection is the practice of gathering information from public websites and web services at scale, usually by automated means, to build datasets that feed research, analytics and machine learning.

sections.body: Alternative data means information generated as a byproduct of ordinary activity rather than for investors: satellite pictures of parking lots, card swipes, ship transponder pings, phone location traces, scraped web pages. Artificial intelligence is what makes this material usable, because the raw feeds are noisy, huge and unlabeled. Computer vision counts cars and tracks construction progress from orbit, while sequence models turn transaction streams into estimates of a retailer's sales before the company reports them. Funds, insurers and logistics firms now run these pipelines as routine inputs, not experiments. The work is measurement and inference: turning a physical or commercial trace into a number someone can act on.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Satellite imagery is the most mature area, with regular revisit times and models that detect change reliably, though cloud cover and resolution still limit what can be seen. Card data is widely used but panel bias is unsolved, since the sample of spenders is never a clean mirror of a company's customers, and privacy rules keep shifting what can be bought. Shipping and sensor feeds are strong where hardware is standardized and patchy where it is not. Location data has degraded as operating systems tightened permission and identifiers, so panels shrank and long histories broke. Web collection works well at scale but is legally contested and brittle against site changes. None of these sources is a clean measurement, and treating any of them as ground truth is the common failure.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages here follow the data from sky to screen. Satellite Imagery covers overhead sensing, the oldest and most visual of the sources, and is where a reader should start to understand change detection. Card Transaction Data deals with consumer spending panels and the panel bias problem that dominates any revenue estimate built from them. Sensor and Shipping Data moves to industrial and freight telemetry, where physical sensors and vessel tracking produce the supply side picture. Mobile Location Data explains foot traffic and the privacy driven collapse of the identifiers that made it work. Web Data Collection closes the set with scraping, pricing and job postings, the cheapest source and the one most exposed to legal and technical disruption. Read together they show how separate traces get combined into a single view of economic activity.
